brewing.notes: A safe starting point for raw pu-erh: rinse once, gongfu style, short early steeps.

description:
A heavily compressed discus in the Red Mark family of vintage Yunnan pu-erh, made as a special order.

This is a way of preparing tea more than a tea you buy under one name, so the recipe and the base tea change from one maker to the next.
history: It was made mostly in the early 1950s, and the hard pressing was meant to ease shipping. That pressing altered how the tea fermented with age, giving it a flavour apart from other Red Mark teas. Little more is documented.
processing: Pressed harder than ordinary Red Mark cakes, which changes its later fermentation.
harvest_season: Not tied to a harvest: it depends on the base tea.
appearance_dry: Usually a pressed cake of silvery-green to brown leaf, darkening with age.
appearance_liquor: Usually pale gold when young, deepening to amber with age.
taste_profile: Expect what young raw pu-erh usually gives: bright, bitter-sweet and full, mellowing with age.
